title: Improved Convergence of Carleman-Embedded Quantum Algorithm for the Vlasov-Poisson System
authors: Matthew Christensen, Tom Goffrey, Animesh Datta
abstract: We extend the regime of convergence of Carleman-embedded quantum algorithms that solve the Vlasov-Poisson equations from kinetic plasma physics. We establish convergence, using both analytical and numerical lower bounds, for physically reasonable collision frequencies using a Fourier-Hermite expansion of the shifted phase-space distribution function. We also show that for a large class of basis functions, the convergence of the Carleman-embedded Vlasov-Poisson system requires increasing collision frequency strength with velocity resolution. The complexity of the quantum algorithm depends strongly on whether we seek time-averaged or -resolved outputs.
summary: The paper analyzes the convergence limits of quantum algorithms applied to solve the Vlasov-Poisson equation from kinetic theory. By employing Carleman embedding and Fourier-Hermite expansions, the authors derive new lower bounds on the necessary collision frequency for stable simulation. This advances both the theoretical understanding of plasma dynamics and the practical feasibility of simulating such systems using quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is extending the convergence regime of quantum algorithms designed to solve the Vlasov-Poisson equations from kinetic plasma physics.
main_result: Convergence is established for physically reasonable collision frequencies, improving upon previous requirements for unphysically large dissipation. The quantum algorithm shows a potential speedup over classical methods for time-averaged outputs.
method: The authors employ Carleman embedding to transform the infinite-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson system into a finite-dimensional linear system suitable for quantum simulation analysis, using Fourier-Hermite expansions.
model_or_system: The model is the Vlasov-Poisson system, specifically analyzed in its collisional form incorporating a BGK collision operator. The dynamics are discretized via a Fourier-Hermite expansion of the shifted phase-space distribution function.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on using a Fourier-Hermite expansion for the distribution function and making assumptions about the form of the Lyapunov functions ($P$). A key limitation is that convergence might require increasing collision frequency strength with velocity resolution.

paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the mathematical framework by expanding the Vlasov-Poisson system into ODEs for coefficients. It then applies Carleman embedding to form linear/nonlinear matrices ($F_1, F_2$). The core analysis involves minimizing Lyapunov function bounds over various parameters to determine the minimum required collision frequency ($
u_P$) for convergence.
why_interesting: This work bridges advanced quantum simulation techniques (Carleman embedding) with fundamental plasma physics problems. For AMO/open systems, it provides a rigorous framework for analyzing the stability and computational feasibility of simulating complex, dissipative, nonlinear dynamics using quantum resources.
